title: Dow Slides Red Amid Rate Shock Fears; Nvidia Falls as Anthropic IPO Looms
body:
Wall Street slipped into the red on Wednesday after a senior Federal Reserve official hinted that policymakers may need to deliver a “shock” rate hike to rein in stubborn inflation, a prospect that rattled risk‑on investors. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 0.7%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite fell 0.9% and 1.2% respectively. Technology heavyweight Nvidia, which has been the market’s biggest driver of recent gains, tumbled more than 3% after analysts warned that the looming initial public offering of AI start‑up Anthropic could intensify competition in the generative‑AI space.

The comments came from Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who told a congressional hearing that the central bank might need to act more aggressively than previously signaled to prevent inflation from becoming entrenched. Although he stopped short of specifying a timeline, the suggestion of a “shock” move—typically understood as a sudden, sizable increase in the policy rate—prompted traders to price in a higher probability of a 75‑basis‑point hike at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting. Treasury yields rose across the curve, with the 10‑year note climbing to 4.62%, a level not seen since early 2023, further weighing on equity valuations.

Nvidia’s slide was amplified by concerns that the AI sector could face a wave of new entrants. Anthropic, backed by major investors including Google’s parent Alphabet, is slated to go public later this year with a valuation that could exceed $20 billion. The prospect of a well‑funded rival offering comparable large‑language‑model services threatens to dilute Nvidia’s market share and pricing power. While the chipmaker posted a record‑breaking quarter earlier this month, its shares have become increasingly sensitive to any hint of competitive pressure, especially as its stock price already reflects a hefty premium built on expectations of perpetual growth.

Broader market sentiment echoed the Fed’s cautionary tone. Defensive sectors such as utilities and consumer staples outperformed, with the Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF gaining 0.4% as investors rotated into perceived safe havens. Conversely, growth‑oriented names—particularly those with high price‑to‑earnings multiples—saw sharper declines. The Nasdaq’s performance underscores the vulnerability of tech‑heavy portfolios to macro‑policy shifts, a pattern that has recurred since the Federal Reserve began tightening in early 2022.

Analysts note that the market’s reaction may be more about the uncertainty surrounding the timing and magnitude of future rate moves than about a definitive policy change. “Investors are pricing in a higher risk of a steep rate hike, which compresses the valuation cushion for growth stocks,” said Karen Liu, senior equity strategist at Meridian Capital. “If the Fed does indeed deliver a shock, we could see a more pronounced rotation toward value and dividend‑paying stocks, while the AI hype cycle may temper until clearer guidance emerges.”

Looking ahead, traders will monitor the upcoming Fed meeting minutes for clues about the central bank’s inflation outlook, as well as the scheduled release of corporate earnings from other AI‑related firms. Should the Fed adopt a more aggressive stance, the ripple effects could extend beyond equities, influencing credit spreads and currency markets. Meanwhile, the anticipation surrounding Anthropic’s IPO adds another layer of complexity, potentially reshaping the competitive dynamics of the AI industry. In this environment, investors are likely to remain cautious, balancing the allure of high‑growth tech opportunities against the backdrop of an uncertain monetary policy trajectory.
